_comment: Linux (Debian) patch policy for the port flow (fieldkit build-harness start firefox). Derived 2026-10-14 from the Windows machine's config/patch_policy.json: same groups, same order, Linux statuses. The Windows file disabled 01.MEDIA and excluded the GTK, socket and font patches because they are Linux code; here they are the point. Every status carries its reason; change the reason when you change the status.
_fuzz_note: patch --fuzz=3 as on Windows (recreate_success.sh lineage). The replay proof applies with --fuzz=0 and is the stricter judge of the exported set.

01.MEDIA.reason: VA-API / VDPAU / PulseAudio: the Linux media group. Disabled on Windows (DXVA2/WASAPI), it is the reason this build exists on Linux: hardware H.264 only, the 6-layer codec gate (GOLDEN_RULES).
01.MEDIA.platforms_why: Recorded in this group's reason and in commit 57bad03 (the Windows policy, never published, had it disabled): Windows decodes through DXVA2/WASAPI. The harness reads this field on every platform (fieldkit firefox.for_platform), so the Windows port no longer needs its own policy file.
01.MEDIA.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

02.GPU.reason: Gecko's graphics blocklist patches, cross-platform; on Linux widget/gtk/GfxInfo.cpp is included (Windows excluded it).

03.NETWORKING.reason: C++ patches in netwerk/. nsSocketTransport2.cpp was excluded on Windows; on Linux it is applied and must be verified against 158 (first port).
03.NETWORKING.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

04.PERFORMANCE.reason: Expected platform-neutral (Windows verified nothing assumes a Linux scheduler; here the scheduler IS Linux).

05.PREFS.reason: Baked-in prefs. NEW_FILES carries a mozconfig that is NOT used: the Linux build uses the repository's mozconfig (clang-21, lld, sccache, Wayland).
05.PREFS.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

07.TOOLKIT.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

08.Look.reason: Locale patches and the browser/branding/gorilla tree. Windows installer assets inside it are inert on Linux; the .deb takes its icon from deb_template.
08.Look.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

09.REMOTE.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

10.OVERRIDES.reason: NEW_FILES only (user.js); apply.sh never copies user.js into the tree.

11.FONT.SYSTEM.reason: The font system: Microsoft fonts are fetched by scripts/fonts-microsoft.sh and shipped inside the .deb (settled 2026-08-03); browser/fonts/moz.build is included here (Windows excluded it).

12.MOZAMBIQUE.DRILL.reason: RecipeRunner / RemoteSettingsExperimentLoader timer neutralisation, cross-platform JS.

13.TELEMETRY.KILL.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

14.EGRESS.LOCKDOWN.reason: No .patch files; documentation or NEW_FILES only.

16.SNAPSHOT.DELTA.2026-08-12.reason: The 2026-08-12 completeness sweep from the LINUX build tree: one patch per changed file. The generated activity-stream bundle stays excluded (generated output, regenerate instead); the dom/media patches Windows excluded are Linux media and are included.
16.SNAPSHOT.DELTA.2026-08-12.exclude_reason_tokens: 2026-10-14: the three design-token patches are 155-era copies. Fable, patch 21.PORT.FIXES.157/078: 'For a later Firefox: drop the three 16.SNAPSHOT tokens-*.css patches and this one; keep step 2.' The token files stay pristine; 079 lays the Gorilla dark look on top.
16.SNAPSHOT.DELTA.2026-08-12.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

20.SNAPSHOT.DELTA.155.0.1.reason: The 155.0.1 snapshot delta the 157 port started from: bundled uBlock Origin, the AIWindow stub, built-in extensions. Platform-neutral.
20.SNAPSHOT.DELTA.155.0.1.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

21.PORT.FIXES.157.reason: The 157 port's repairs, exported by the harness on Windows: excision creep, a misplaced hunk, a broken override. Cross-platform source.
21.PORT.FIXES.157.exclude_reason: 078 put the token files back to pristine 157; on any later Firefox they are pristine already. Its own header: 'drop the three 16.SNAPSHOT tokens-*.css patches and this one; keep step 2' (079).
21.PORT.FIXES.157.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

22.EGRESS.LOCKDOWN.157.reason: Every privacy cut made in source for 157 (telemetry, Remote Settings, Normandy, hidden about: pages). Cross-platform; 80 patches, 57 files touched by more than one patch: a stacked series, apply in order only.
22.EGRESS.LOCKDOWN.157.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

21.PORT.FIXES.158.reason: The 158 port's repairs and Gorilla changes made on the Linux 158 tree (2026-10-14/15), exported by build-harness export-hand: build fixes for 158 API moves, the GPU blocklist unlock carried from 155, About stamp, Settings layout, the single search engine. Cross-platform source unless a patch names its platform.
21.PORT.FIXES.158.exclude_on_why: Windows excluded browser/fonts/moz.build (the Linux Microsoft-font listing) and widget/gtk/GfxInfo.cpp (GTK only) in its own policy (commit 57bad03). The shared GPU unlock (GfxInfoBase.cpp, GfxDriverInfo.cpp) applies on both (must_keep, D-158-06).
21.PORT.FIXES.158.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

22.EGRESS.LOCKDOWN.158.reason: Privacy cuts and lockdowns made on the 158 tree (2026-10-14/15): AI features excised (D-158-08), Smart Window removed, GenAI startup hook, Sync promo, add-on refusal message (D-157-05). Deleted files are listed in DELETED_FILES.manifest.txt. Cross-platform; apply in order.
22.EGRESS.LOCKDOWN.158.exclude_reason_158: Superseded for Firefox 158: does not apply to pristine 158; the file's 158 form is in 23.REBASE.158 (rebase-set). Kept on disk as history.

23.REBASE.158.reason: Generated by build-harness rebase-set: the step from the rest of the set to the tree built for Firefox 158, for every platform. Applied after every hand-made group. Proven by replay (same git tree hash).

23.REBASE.158.linux.reason: Generated by build-harness rebase-set on linux: the files a linux-only part of the set touches. Applied last, on linux only.

must_keep._why: Files the shared patch set must always carry, whichever platform regenerates it. 2026-10-03 (commit 1070063) the set was rebuilt from the Windows 157 tree and 83 patch files vanished, among them the Linux GPU unlock and the font listing, while the prose above still promised them. Checked before every build by the Fieldkit preflight row must-keep (the patch exists in patches/ and the tree changes the file).

files.why: GPU blocklist unlock, GTK layer: old Intel/AMD/NVIDIA keep hardware video decode and WebRender
GPU blocklist short-circuit, shared layer (Linux and Windows)
Sandy/Ivy Bridge device families taken off the blocklist (Linux and Windows)
the Microsoft fonts are listed so they ship inside the .deb

binary_exempt.browser/branding/gorilla/wizHeader.bmp: Windows NSIS installer bitmap, not used by the Linux build. The set's delta payload is corrupt: `git apply --check` says 'corrupt binary patch' (2026-10-15, binary-patches audit). The Windows harness must re-export it from its tree; on Windows this exemption does not apply.

_binary_exempt_note: binary_exempt {path: reason}: a GIT binary patch section a person decided this platform does without. Read by fieldkit build-harness binary-patches and the preflight row binary-patches (BLOCKER otherwise).
